rv.q: Mix that with the incessant weakness of the script’s plays on words and there is really nothing to have faith in.
If, as Sinyor says in his programme notes, we all need to learn to laugh at God, this certainly isn’t the place to start.
It is also patchy, childish and overlong, and it ultimately collapses under the weight of its own – and our – expectations.
NotMoses is funny and fun, but like the speed of its one liners it’s easily forgotten.

cn.t: Critics mostly pan this biblical comedy as a poor man's Life of Brian—flat jokes, weak satire, and a "bad sixth-form revue" feel. One reviewer finds charm in its gag-a-minute energy, but the majority agree it fails to deliver.
